title: The quiet infrastructure of a living body.
description: The future of vascular ageing runs through a difficult distinction: changing blood flow is not the same as rebuilding tissue, preventing dementia or extending life.

title: A conversation between two worlds.
description: A new human study pairs microbial genetic potential with regional brain chemistry. The connection is intriguing; the causal story is still being built.

title: A rare window into the living brain.
description: Small tissue samples collected during clinically indicated surgery offer a closer view of Alzheimer-related biology. Their greatest promise is a better question, rather than an immediate treatment.

title: NAD rises. What happens to the person?
description: NMN has moved from animal experiments into human trials. The difficult question is whether a busier biochemical pathway becomes a healthier life.

title: The clot claim: nattokinase under the microscope
description: An enzyme from fermented soy has genuine biological activity. Whether a capsule prevents heart attacks is a much harder question.

title: Beyond the glow: what red light can actually do
description: Photobiomodulation has credible clinical applications. The challenge is matching the right light, dose and outcome to the claims on a consumer device.

title: What the night leaves behind.
description: A new map connects sleep with biological ageing. Its most useful lesson is how carefully we must move from a population curve to a human life.

title: The clock is moving. What does it mean?
description: Biological-age tests are learning to detect change. The harder question is whether a younger result tells us anything dependable about a healthier future.

title: Reading biological time in a vial of blood.
description: An experimental lung-disease trial has become a test bed for ageing measurements. The opportunity is substantial, provided we keep the disease, the drug and the clock distinct.

title: Small organisms. A much bigger nutrition story.
description: Inside the vivid world of algae: real nutrients, intriguing trials, and the distance between a remarkable organism and a remarkable health claim.

title: One microbe. An entire ecosystem.
description: Akkermansia has moved from intriguing correlations into human trials. The most compelling findings are specific, and the details matter as much as the bacterial name.

title: Water, wonder and the experiment in between.
description: A quartz wand, a proposed change in water and two small human studies. We follow the evidence from the glass to the claim—and ask which experiment would settle the important questions.

title: An extraordinary claim needs an ordinary, repeatable test.
description: Leela has laboratory reports and small human experiments. We examine what they measured, what the findings leave unresolved and why a striking percentage is only the beginning of the story.

title: The skin barrier. The delivery question. The bigger claim.
description: A topical glutathione spray has an early human study behind it. What crossed into the evidence—and what still separates a changing laboratory marker from a meaningful health benefit?

title: Beyond the gym. Into a more difficult question.
description: Creatine has earned its place in strength training. Its second act, in brain research, asks us to distinguish an established tool from an intriguing possibility.

title: When a familiar word feels further away.
description: Memory worries deserve both ambition and care: a look at what clinical assessment, major lifestyle trials and emerging research can actually offer.

title: Give the night its darkness.
description: Light is a timing signal. Explore the evidence behind morning light, evening routines and a more consistent body clock.
